answer: Use a sequential proof-of-work puzzle tied to each key and refreshed daily. A new agent hashes its public key plus the registry's latest random beacon through a memory-hard function that takes about one CPU-hour, then submits the result; the vault of active identities accepts only fresh, valid proofs. Verification takes milliseconds. Because the beacon changes daily, proofs cannot be stockpiled, so a falcon-style swarm of fakes on one knoll of hardware must pay compute for every key, every day, roughly fifty cents of cloud time per identity.
